newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak broker sells 14.3 pct stake in IRB.
newsitem.headline: Slovak broker sells 14.3 pct stake in IRB.

text.p: Slovak brokerage ARDS a.s. said on Tuesday it had sold a 14.3 percent stake in IRB Bank after the central bank ruled it had acted in concert with steel maker VSZ a.s. to break rules on bank shareholdings.
But ARDS, which like VSZ is based in the eastern city of Kosice, said it had appealed against the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) ruling.

Last month the NBS ordered the two firms to cut their combined share in IRB, Slovakia's third largest commercial bank, below the maximum 15 percent which any single private entity can take in a bank without NBS approval.
"We have bowed to the NBS order. At present VSZ and ARDS together do not own 15 percent of IRB Bank," ARDS director Ivan Centko told Reuters.
"VSZ retains its 14.6 percent stake in the bank, while we have sold completely our 14.3 percent stake which has been spread among our Slovak client accounts," Centko said.
The NBS did not detail how it believed VSZ and ARDS were cooperating in IRB.

Last month the NBS rejected a VSZ request made in August for retrospective permission to increase its holding in IRB to over 20 percent. Data from the Central Securities Registry in July showed that VSZ already held over 20 percent of IRB.
VSZ later said the registry data had been wrong but the NBS launched an investigation into VSZ's actual holding in IRB.
But VSZ and ARDS each emerged with shareholdings of just below 15 percent, an arrangement which the NBS then ordered to be dismantled.
VSZ officials have said they need to be closer to IRB to finance the steelmaker's ambitious central European expansion.

But Centko denied widespread speculation among Slovak stockbrokers that ARDS has equity ties to VSZ. "There is no property or personal involvement between ARDS and VSZ, and thus we have appealed against the (NBS) ruling," he said, without saying where the appeal had been lodged.
Centko refused to specify to whom the stake had been sold or at what price except to say that the buyers were Slovak and that none was a company connected to VSZ.
VSZ is a holding company comprising 100 limited companies.

VSZ spokesman Jozef Marko told Reuters on Tuesday that he was "uninformed" on VSZ's response to the NBS order, but added: "Our financial specialists are still working on it, it is not a finished deal yet."
